label: echoed g in early copy phase (g from original positions 1-3)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is g, i.e. the model is re-reading a g that was original token 1, 2 or 3 (recall_idx 2-4), and at least one output still remains. Never fires during the original phase or on the delimiter, and essentially never on any token other than g. Magnitude is largest when the g was original token 1 (recall_idx 2: about 42% of activations but 57% of activation mass, and all top examples look like x g ... <DEL> x [g]). It is weaker for g at positions 2-3, and very weak or absent for g at position 0 (the input right after <DEL>), for g at positions 4 and later, and on the final step (to_go = 0). Remaining false positives are mostly g at original position 3 in longer sequences.

issues: I reproduced the reported test scores exactly: P 0.912, R 0.970, F1 0.940, mass recall 0.997.
Phase claims hold. The feature never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter (0 activations), and 38525 of the 38527 dev activations have in_tok == g.

Precision of 'copy phase and in_tok == g' broken down by recall_idx: 1 → 0.05, 2 → 0.96, 3 → 0.85, 4 → 0.56, 5 → 0.008. Mass share: recall_idx 2 has 0.565 and recall_idx 3 has 0.382. This matches the claimed peak at original position 1 and the near-absence at positions 0 and 4+.
to_go = 0 almost never fires (precision 0.0 to 0.05 for recall_idx 2-4). For recall_idx 2-3 with to_go >= 1, precision is about 1.0, so the to_go >= 1 condition is justified.

Remaining false positives are concentrated at recall_idx 4 (g at original position 3). Precision there is 0.55 to 0.76 at every L and to_go, and no history variable separates firing from non-firing cases: in_count 0.70/0.60, prev_tok digit or vowel 0.64/0.71, n_digits 0.63/0.72, next_out digit 0.77. Activations in this cell are weak (5% of mass), so this looks like a graded weak response cut off by the activation threshold, not a missing rule. The explanation already describes it accurately.
Missed activations: 1139 test steps holding 0.3% of activation mass, all low magnitude (g at original position 0, at position 4+, or on the last step). This is scattered noise.
Top examples all have the form 'x g ... <DEL> x [g]', as claimed. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
